- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underreact — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% relative to recent mean.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overcorrects downward — reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day post-spike.  
- If supply net is strongly negative (e.g., < -15) and sentiment is bearish, model underestimates downside — add 2–5% buffer below forecast mean.  
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d), model over-optimistically assumes trend continuation — cap forecast growth at 0.5% per day max.  
- When sentiment flips from bullish to bearish (e.g., -0.5 to 0.0), model lags — delay forecast drop by 1–2 days and reduce slope by 0.3–0.7% per day.  
- If true outcome deviates >10% from 30d mean, check sentiment history for “reversal” signals — if present, apply mean reversion rule: forecast = 30d mean ± 2×std dev.
